name: Unit Tests CI
on: push: branches: [ master, main, develop ] pull_request: branches: [ master, main ]
permissions: contents: read checks: write pull-requests: write
env: ORTOOLS_IMAGE: ghcr.io/mertbiyikli/ortools:linux ORTOOLS_CACHE: ghcr.io/mertbiyikli/ortools:linux-cache
jobs: build-and-test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4
- name: Login to GHCR uses: docker/login-action@v3 with: registry: ghcr.io username: ${{ github.repository_owner }} password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
- name: Pull OR-Tools image run: docker pull $ORTOOLS_IMAGE
- name: Build and Run Tests run: | docker run --rm \ -v ${{ github.workspace }}:/app \ -w /app \ $ORTOOLS_IMAGE \ bash -c " cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \ -DUSE_OPENMP=ON \ -DBUILD_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build -j\$(nproc) && cd build && ctest --output-on-failure --verbose "
- name: Upload Test Results if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: test-results path: build/test_results/ retention-days: 30
- name: Publish Test Results if: always() uses: EnricoMi/publish-unit-test-result-action@v2 with: files: build/test_results/*.xml check_name: Unit Test Results

# Unit Tests Quick Start Guide
## Overview
This project includes a comprehensive unit test suite using Catch2 with tests for: - **GraphCSR**: Compressed Sparse Row graph representation - **GraphADJ**: Adjacency list graph representation - **FastCKR**: Fast CKR tree metric algorithm - **FRT**: FRT tree metric algorithm - **ElectricalFlow**: Laplacian solver for electrical flow - **RoutingTable**: All-pair and linear routing tables
## Quick Start
### Option 1: Using the Test Runner Script (Recommended)
```bash # Make sure you're in the project root directory cd /Users/halilibrahim/Desktop/Thesis/ObliviousRouting
# Run all tests ./scripts/run_tests.sh
# Run only specific tests ./scripts/run_tests.sh -f GraphCSR
# Run with verbose output ./scripts/run_tests.sh -v
# Clean rebuild ./scripts/run_tests.sh -c
# Debug mode ./scripts/run_tests.sh --debug ```
### Option 2: Manual CMake Build
```bash # Configure cmake -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -S . -B build_tests
# Build cmake --build build_tests -j$(nproc)
# Run tests cd build_tests && ctest --output-on-failure ```
### Option 3: Direct Test Executable
```bash # Build cmake -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -S . -B build_tests cmake --build build_tests
# Run all tests ./build_tests/unit_tests
# Run specific test category ./build_tests/unit_tests "[GraphCSR]"
# Run specific test ./build_tests/unit_tests "GraphCSR - Edge Addition"
# Verbose output ./build_tests/unit_tests -v
# Generate XML report ./build_tests/unit_tests -r xml -o test_results.xml ```
## Test Categories
Run tests by category:
```bash ./build_tests/unit_tests "[GraphCSR]" # CSR graph tests ./build_tests/unit_tests "[GraphADJList]" # Adjacency list tests ./build_tests/unit_tests "[FastCKR]" # FastCKR tests ./build_tests/unit_tests "[FRT]" # FRT tests ./build_tests/unit_tests "[LaplacianSolver]" # Electrical flow tests ./build_tests/unit_tests "[RoutingTable]" # Routing table tests ```
## Test Execution
### Run All Tests ```bash cd build_tests ctest ```
### Run with Detailed Output ```bash cd build_tests ctest --output-on-failure ctest -VV # Very verbose ```
### Run Specific Tests ```bash # By name pattern ctest -R "Shortest Path" -V
# By category ctest -R "GraphCSR" -V
# Exclude tests ctest -E "Large Graph" -V ```
### Generate Reports ```bash # JUnit XML format (for CI/CD) ctest -R ".*" --output-on-failure -O test_output.xml
# CTest output format ctest --output-on-failure > test_results.txt ```
## Project Structure
``` ObliviousRouting/ ├── tests/ # Test directory │ ├── test_main.cpp # Test entry point │ ├── test_graph_csr.cpp # CSR graph tests (13 tests) │ ├── test_graph_adj.cpp # Adjacency list tests (11 tests) │ ├── test_fast_ckr.cpp # FastCKR tests (11 tests) │ ├── test_frt.cpp # FRT tests (12 tests) │ ├── test_electrical_flow.cpp # Laplacian solver tests (11 tests) │ ├── test_routing_table.cpp # Routing table tests (22 tests) │ └── README_TESTS.md # Detailed test documentation ├── scripts/ │ └── run_tests.sh # Test runner script ├── .github/workflows/ │ ├── ci.yml # Main CI workflow (includes tests) │ └── tests.yml # Dedicated test workflow └── CMakeLists.txt # Test configuration ```
## Statistics
- **Total Tests**: 80+ - **Test Files**: 6 - **Test Categories**: 6 - **Code Coverage**: Covers major data structures and algorithms
## Common Issues and Solutions
### Issue: "Catch2 not found" **Solution**: CMake will automatically fetch Catch2. Ensure internet is available.
### Issue: "Tests take too long" **Solution**: ```bash # Run in parallel ctest -j4 --output-on-failure
# Or use the script ./scripts/run_tests.sh -j8 ```
### Issue: "Specific test fails" **Solution**: ```bash # Run just that test with verbose output ./build_tests/unit_tests "TestName" -v
# Get more details ./build_tests/unit_tests "TestName" --success ```
### Issue: "Memory errors in tests" **Solution**: ```bash # Build in Debug mode with sanitizers ./scripts/run_tests.sh --debug ```
## Continuous Integration
Tests run automatically on: - Every push to `master` - Every pull request - Can be manually triggered
### View CI Results - Visit: `.github/workflows/` for available workflows - Check GitHub Actions tab for run results - Tests must pass before merging to main
## Test Development
### Adding a New Test
1. Create test file in `tests/` directory 2. Follow Catch2 format: ```cpp #include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp> #include "your/header.h"
TEST_CASE("FeatureName - Scenario", "[Category]") { // Setup YourClass obj;
// Test REQUIRE(obj.method() == expected); } ```
3. Add to `CMakeLists.txt` in tests section 4. Run tests to verify
### Best Practices
- Use descriptive test names - Test one thing per test case - Use appropriate assertions: - `REQUIRE()` - fails if false - `CHECK()` - reports but continues - `REQUIRE_THROWS()` - expects exception - Use fixtures for setup/teardown - Test edge cases and normal cases
## Performance Considerations
### Fast Tests Most unit tests complete in < 1ms
### Slower Tests - Graph tests with 100+ nodes: 5-50ms - Solver tests: 10-100ms
### Optimization ```bash # Skip slow tests ctest -E "Large|Performance" --output-on-failure
# Run only fast tests ctest -R "^(?!.*Large)" --output-on-failure ```
## Debugging Failed Tests
### Using GDB ```bash # Run with debugger gdb --args ./build_tests/unit_tests "TestName"
# Run until failure (gdb) run (gdb) bt # Show backtrace (gdb) print variable_name ```
### Using Valgrind ```bash valgrind --leak-check=full ./build_tests/unit_tests "[Category]" ```
### Add Debug Output ```cpp TEST_CASE("Debug Example", "[Debug]") { auto result = function(); std::cout << "Result: " << result << std::endl; REQUIRE(result == expected); } ```
## Integration with CLion
CLion has built-in Catch2 support:
1. Open project in CLion 2. Configure CMake with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON` 3. Right-click test file → Run/Debug tests 4. Use Test Explorer window for navigation
## Integration with VS Code
Install Catch2 extension and: 1. Build tests: `cmake --build . --target unit_tests` 2. Open Test Explorer 3. Click Run on desired test
## Help and Documentation
- **Catch2 Documentation**: https://github.com/catchorg/Catch2/tree/devel/docs - **CMake Testing**: https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/enable_testing.html - **Project Issues**: Check `.github/workflows/` for CI logs
## Next Steps
1. ✅ Set up test environment 2. ✅ Build test suite 3. ✅ Run initial tests 4. Review test output 5. Debug any failures 6. Integrate with your workflow 7. Add more tests as needed
## Quick Command Reference
```bash # Build only cmake --build build_tests
# Run all tests ctest -C build_tests --output-on-failure
# Tests + verbose ctest --output-on-failure -VV
# Specific category ctest -R "GraphCSR" --output-on-failure
# Parallel execution ctest -j4 --output-on-failure
# Stop at first failure ctest --output-on-failure --stop-on-test
# Test runner script ./scripts/run_tests.sh -v -f "GraphCSR" ```
---
**For detailed test documentation**, see `tests/README_TESTS.md`

# Unit Test Suite Implementation Guide

## What Was Implemented
### 1. Test Files (6 files, 88 tests total)
#### `tests/test_graph_csr.cpp` (13 tests) Tests for Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) graph representation: - Basic construction and edge operations - Path finding algorithms (unidirectional and bidirectional) - Edge distance/capacity updates - Performance with large graphs (100+ nodes)
#### `tests/test_graph_adj.cpp` (11 tests) Tests for Adjacency List graph representation: - Adjacency list structure integrity - Multiple edge handling from same node - Distance and capacity operations - Shortest path computation - Algorithm alternatives
#### `tests/test_fast_ckr.cpp` (11 tests) Tests for Fast CKR tree metric algorithm: - Level partition computation - Cluster center selection - Radius constraints (delta/4 to delta/2) - Large graph partitioning - Mendel scaling support
#### `tests/test_frt.cpp` (12 tests) Tests for FRT tree metric algorithm: - Deterministic radius storage (exact delta) - Owner assignment and clustering - Path-based distance calculations - Fully connected graph handling - Multiple delta value variations
#### `tests/test_electrical_flow.cpp` (11 tests) Tests for Electrical Flow computation using Laplacian Solver: - Laplacian matrix construction - Electrical potential solving - Weight updates and recomputation - Dirichlet boundary conditions - Grid graph analysis - Symmetric graph handling
#### `tests/test_routing_table.cpp` (22 tests) Tests for routing table data structures: - AllPairRoutingTable: commodity-based flow storage (12 tests) - LinearRoutingTable: source-based flow storage (10 tests) - Flow addition, retrieval, and removal - Multi-commodity routing scenarios

#### `tests/test_main.cpp` Catch2 test framework entry point

#!/bin/bash
# ObliviousRouting Test Runner Script # This script helps build and run the test suite
set -e # Exit on error
# Colors for output RED='\033[0;31m' GREEN='\033[0;32m' YELLOW='\033[1;33m' NC='\033[0m' # No Color
# Defaults BUILD_DIR="cmake-build-tests" CMAKE_FLAGS="-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release" RUN_TESTS=true VERBOSE=false PARALLEL="" TEST_FILTER=""
# Usage information usage() { echo "Usage: $0 [options]" echo "Options:" echo " -h, --help Show this help message" echo " -b, --build-dir DIR Custom build directory (default: $BUILD_DIR)" echo " -j, --parallel N Number of parallel jobs (default: auto-detect)" echo " -f, --filter PATTERN Run only tests matching pattern" echo " -v, --verbose Verbose test output" echo " -c, --clean Clean build directory before building" echo " --no-test Build only, don't run tests" echo " --debug Build in Debug mode instead of Release" echo "" echo "Examples:" echo " # Build and run all tests" echo " $0" echo "" echo " # Run only graph tests with verbose output" echo " $0 -f GraphCSR -v" echo "" echo " # Build with 4 parallel jobs, don't run tests" echo " $0 -j 4 --no-test" echo "" echo " # Clean build with debug info" echo " $0 -c --debug" }
# Parse arguments while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case $1 in -h|--help) usage exit 0 ;; -b|--build-dir) BUILD_DIR="$2" shift 2 ;; -j|--parallel) PARALLEL="-j$2" shift 2 ;; -f|--filter) TEST_FILTER="$2" shift 2 ;; -v|--verbose) VERBOSE=true shift ;; -c|--clean) echo "Cleaning $BUILD_DIR..." rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR" shift ;; --no-test) RUN_TESTS=false shift ;; --debug) CMAKE_FLAGS="${CMAKE_FLAGS/Release/Debug}" shift ;; *) echo "Unknown option: $1" usage exit 1 ;; esac done
# Detect number of parallel jobs if not specified if [ -z "$PARALLEL" ]; then if command -v nproc &> /dev/null; then PARALLEL="-j$(nproc)" elif [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then PARALLEL="-j$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)" else PARALLEL="-j4" # Fallback fi fi
echo -e "${GREEN}=== ObliviousRouting Test Suite ===${NC}" echo "" echo -e "Configuration:" echo " Build Directory: $BUILD_DIR" echo " CMake Flags: $CMAKE_FLAGS" echo " Parallel Jobs: $PARALLEL" if [ -n "$TEST_FILTER" ]; then echo " Test Filter: $TEST_FILTER" fi echo ""
# Step 1: Configure with CMake echo -e "${YELLOW}[1/3] Configuring CMake...${NC}" cmake -S . -B "$BUILD_DIR" -G Ninja $CMAKE_FLAGS if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo -e "${RED}CMake configuration failed!${NC}" exit 1 fi echo -e "${GREEN}CMake configuration succeeded${NC}" echo ""
# Step 2: Build echo -e "${YELLOW}[2/3] Building tests...${NC}" cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" $PARALLEL if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo -e "${RED}Build failed!${NC}" exit 1 fi echo -e "${GREEN}Build succeeded${NC}" echo ""
# Step 3: Run tests (if enabled) if [ "$RUN_TESTS" = true ]; then echo -e "${YELLOW}[3/3] Running tests...${NC}" echo ""
cd "$BUILD_DIR"
# Build ctest command CTEST_CMD="ctest --output-on-failure"
if [ "$VERBOSE" = true ]; then CTEST_CMD="$CTEST_CMD -VV" fi
if [ -n "$TEST_FILTER" ]; then CTEST_CMD="$CTEST_CMD -R '$TEST_FILTER'" fi
# Add parallel jobs CTEST_CMD="$CTEST_CMD $PARALLEL"
echo "Running: $CTEST_CMD" echo ""
eval "$CTEST_CMD" TEST_RESULT=$?
cd - > /dev/null
if [ $TEST_RESULT -eq 0 ]; then echo "" echo -e "${GREEN}=== All tests passed! ===${NC}" else echo "" echo -e "${RED}=== Some tests failed ===${NC}" echo "" echo "To debug specific test:" echo " $BUILD_DIR/unit_tests '[TestPattern]'" exit 1 fi else echo -e "${GREEN}=== Build completed successfully ===${NC}" echo "" echo "To run tests:" echo " cd $BUILD_DIR && ctest --output-on-failure" echo "Or:" echo " ./$BUILD_DIR/unit_tests" fi
